request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in and sheet loading are in place, and `bin/e2e` passes.

- **Sign in:** you type a name (no password) using `signin-name` and `signin-submit`, and the name then shows in `current-user`.
- **Choosing a sheet:** you type an id into `sheet-id-input` and press `sheet-load`, and the active id shows in `sheet-current-id`. Loading the same id again re-reads it from the store.
- **Server:** there's one new route, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}`, made of two steps (`LoadSheet` then `RespondWithSheet`) in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/`. Loading never writes anything, so an id that was never used comes back as an empty sheet.
- **No database table yet:** a sheet holds no data so far, so there's no migration and nothing is written to the audit file. Later features will add their own tables keyed by sheet id.
- **Where the state lives:** the signed-in name and active sheet are kept in the URL (`?user=…&sheet=…`), following the app's convention. All of this is on the home page in `routes/index.tsx`, with the code in `features/session/`.
- **For later features:** I added an empty slot, `sheet.page` (`slots/defs/sheetPage.ts`), that receives `sheetId` and `user` once a sheet is loaded. Features that work on a sheet can fill it without changing the home page.
- **Existing marker:** the `home-empty` element is still there and now shows until a sheet is loaded.

I also added a `sheet-load-error` message that appears if loading a sheet fails. The test doesn't check it.
